verdict.scope: Design only; final R4 archive manifest is pending and must not be fabricated or bound into source facts yet.
verdict.safety: The separate bounded reader, exact manifest-member hash/size binding, fixed historical source pair, strict command/role/argv/layer validation, and unchanged current readiness boundary form a sound design.
verdict.current_vs_historical: Preserve top-level current Command/Ready as NOT_RUN. Historical derived required readiness is independent and interaction FAIL yields NOT_READY. Pair evidence has an overall FAIL status and contains no readiness field.
verdict.table: Render only the existing eight dimensions (Build, Launch, First frame, Interaction, Exit, Restoration, Visual, Ownership); validate cleanup but do not render it as an added product phase.
verdict.compatibility: Absent optional product_phase_observations must preserve checked-in STATUS bytes exactly.
required_implementation_guards: Require both the outer pair schema termrock-e2e/run03-pair-evidence-v1 and nested receipt.schema termrock-spec/visibility-command-lane-v1; the archived object uses both.
Require exactly one RUN-03 row and reject duplicate matches; add a dedicated duplicate-row negative fixture.
Make the fixed required-phase set and the FAIL/BLOCKED-to-NOT_READY predicate explicit in implementation/tests; do not let NOT_APPLICABLE ownership imply readiness.
Keep the old status-source-archive-20261009 reader unchanged; enforce component-wise no-follow reads and bounded manifest/member/aggregate sizes for the new reports/** reader.
Continue to defer source-facts pinning until the reviewed archive publication provides the final manifest hash and byte count.

tests_expected: optional-field absence preserves exact report bytes
historical RUN-03 row renders with fixed source pair and phase states
wrong source pair or command rejected
historical interaction failure yields NOT_READY without changing current NOT_RUN readiness
limits: No source facts, code, canonical files, Cargo, or tests changed/run.
This is not archive publication, execution approval, or product qualification.
